thread:
anita-pm: Quick design check — dropped a new Figma frame for the policies canvas: https://figma.com/file/XXXX. Can we do a 15m async review? :wave:

marta: :eyes: skimmed. Love the compact rule cards. Two quick things: priority visibility and what happens when rules overlap.

devon-designer: Re: priority, I added a persistent numeric badge on the left of each card (1 / 2 / 3). It should be editable inline. Thinking about affordance for drag vs keyboard reorder.

sam-ux: Capture note — keyboard reorder is a must for a11y and devs who prefer keyboard flows. Proposed shortcut: focus → press Space to lift → Up/Down to move → Space to drop. Show live hint in the toolbar.

lee-frontend: Implementation notes: continuous drag ordering on a virtualized list is expensive. If we do lift/commit model it maps to our existing drag layer and avoids re-render churn. For keyboard we can reuse aria-grabbed and move with mutate order API. Will need explicit focus management so focus doesn't disappear after move.

zoe-a11y: A few accessibility nits:
- Priority badge needs 4.5:1 contrast against the grey background.
- When a rule is removed or disabled, announce "Rule X removed" in an aria-live region.
- For the preview simulator, announce "Simulation complete: N matched, M unmatched" and read top match.
Also prefer not to rely on color only for match/highlight states.

anita-pm: Copy question: validation messages currently show "Invalid rule" — can we be more actionable? Suggestion: "Rule won't match any traffic — check conditions or remove."

devon-designer: Agreed. I pushed copy variants in figma: "No requests will match this rule. Refine conditions or move it lower in priority." and a shorter inline: "No matches — refine conditions." Which should we show where?
- Inline badge: shorter
- Full toast/tooltip: longer with link to examples

marta: Inline short copy + a hover tooltip that shows the long explanation (and a link to our heuristics doc). :+1:

lee-frontend: For validation errors we should also attach a small `?` icon that opens the example modal. Also we'll need programmatic error flags in the API: `validation: {level: "warning"|"error", code: "no_match"}` — can design map to affordances.

anita-pm: Good — Devs, can you make sure the API flag names are stable? We want to use them for rollout gating.

lee-frontend: I'll propose `validation_state` with values `ok`, `warn`, `error` and `validation_code` as string. Will align with backend.

sam-ux: Preview simulator behavior — currently it shows a single matched route. Ask: should it show top 3 matches and explain why the top one was chosen? I think transparency helps debugging.

devon-designer: UI idea: stacked mini-cards in the preview modal showing matched route, score, and which clause matched (header/body/query). Click a card to highlight the originating rule in the canvas. Also include token/time estimates for cost.

zoe-a11y: When clicking a preview card, ensure focus moves to the highlighted rule and that highlight is perceivable via both outline + subtle background (not color only). Also add `aria-describedby` linking the preview card to the rule summary.

lee-frontend: Sounds doable. For highlighting we should set `inert` on other interactive parts while preview modal is open to prevent accidental keyboard actions. Also when we navigate from preview card to canvas, we need to trap focus and then restore focus back to the preview origin on close.

anita-pm: Small ux polish: when a rule is disabled but still higher priority, visually dim it and show a small pill "disabled". Do not change numbering — keep numbering stable so references in runbooks don't break.

devon-designer: Will implement dim + pill. Also adding an optional pin icon to freeze a rule's position (pinning retains its absolute priority and makes it non-droppable). Thoughts?

marta: Pinning could be powerful but also confusing. If we add pin, we need clear copy: "Pinned rules stay fixed at this priority until unpinned." and a tooltip on what happens during reorder and simulations.

zoe-a11y: If pinning exists, ensure keyboard users can toggle pin with a shortcut and that screen readers announce pin state changes.

aria-bot: simulation-bot: Simulation run complete — sample run 2025-12-10T15:03:45Z — 24 requests tested, 6 matched. Top match: rule #2 (user-agent contains "MobileApp").

anita-pm: Nice — include that exact text in the preview modal's summary and a copy button so SEs can paste into tickets.

lee-frontend: One more technical constraint: we can't show live token estimates for full corpora in the modal (costly). We'll show a sampled estimate and label it "sampled estimate" with a tooltip explaining sampling.

devon-designer: Final ask from design side: add an inline validation icon on each rule that expands into a small inline panel with the failing condition highlighted (so users don't have to open rule editor to see what's wrong).

sam-ux: Agree. Quick research note: in tests, reducing clicks by 1.2 on average improves fix rate. Inline panels help.

marta: OK team — action items: devon to iterate figma with these copy/affordance changes; lee to draft keyboard aria patterns + API field names; zoe to write short a11y checklist we can include in the PR; sam to add the preview microcopy to the research notes. I'll consolidate and schedule a 15m sync if needed. :calendar:

anita-pm: Thank you everyone. Will add the link to the heuristics doc in the figma prototypes and tag you. :heart:
